messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate on /v2/generate (model: epsilon-1-quant, region: us-west-2). 5xx rate spiked from 0.5% -> 12% in last 3m. Paging maya (oncall) :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): on it. seeing a lot of customer reports in /support. can someone paste recent logs?

ashley (sre): digging in. quick summary:
- spikes correlate with requests to epsilon-1-quant in us-west-2, particularly long-context requests (>2048).
- kernel logs show repeated "KV_CACHE_MISS and subsequent OOM fallback" on a subset of pods -> causes 500s.
- hosts affected: usw2-ep-03, 05, 07 (3/8 in pool).
logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T18:01:12Z host=usw2-ep-05 model=epsilon-1-quant seq=4096 err="cuda out of memory" fallback=1
2026-03-15T18:01:12Z host=usw2-ep-05 request_id=r87623 status=500 msg="execution failed after quant-kernel" 
```

kevin (eng-runtime): possible causes: a new kernel selection change landed in last rollout that favors aggressive KV prefetch for quantized variants. If that hits long contexts it can spike memory. I want to avoid rollback of infra if we can route traffic off the risky variant. Proposed live mitigation path: 1) apply emergency per-key throttles for heavy keys 2) immediately route traffic away from epsilon-1-quant to epsilon-stable-v3 (FP16) as fallback 3) disable the variant until we have a fix and postmortem.

maya (oncall): agree. do the minimal invasive steps first. kevin, can you push the routing change? ashley, please prepare key throttles for top offending API keys. santosh - can you coordinate customer comms if impact remains?

kevin (eng-runtime): executing routing change now. command:
```
# route 100% traffic from epsilon-1-quant -> epsilon-stable-v3 in us-west-2
redwoodctl traffic-shift --region=us-west-2 --from-model=epsilon-1-quant --to-model=epsilon-stable-v3 --percent=100 --reason="emergency-5xx-2140001234"
```

deploy-bot: ACTION: traffic-shift job queued id=ts-2140001234. expect completion ~30s.

deploy-bot: SUCCESS: traffic-shift ts-2140001234 completed. previous weights: epsilon-1-quant=78%, epsilon-stable-v3=22% -> new weights: epsilon-1-quant=0%, epsilon-stable-v3=100% (us-west-2)

olivia (support): initial customer triage: ~12 support threads affected, highest impact customers: acme-app (high volume), learnly (medium). some errors are transient after retry but ~20% of requests still failing for acme-app before shift.

maya (oncall): good. ashley, start per-key throttles on the heavy hitters while we keep variant disabled. list of top keys from metrics?

ashley (sre): top offending keys by rps: api-acme-01 (42% of failing requests), api-learn-09 (10%), api-devtests (8%). Applying emergency quotas now:
```
# emergency quotas
redwoodctl quota update --key=api-acme-01 --max-rpm=120 --reason="mitigation-2140001234"
redwoodctl quota update --key=api-learn-09 --max-rpm=40 --reason="mitigation-2140001234"
redwoodctl quota update --key=api-devtests --max-rpm=10 --reason="mitigation-2140001234"
```

deploy-bot: QUOTA_CHANGE: applied for api-acme-01, api-learn-09, api-devtests.

maya (oncall): noting customer impact: acme-app reduced error surface after throttles + routing; please prepare a brief for CS to send: what happened + how we mitigated + ETA for reenable. santosh, want me to draft?

santosh (product): pls draft and share. I'll join customer calls if needed. main ask from customers: ETA for full service on epsilon-1-quant or will you keep on stable variant?

kevin (eng-runtime): recommended next steps (short term): keep epsilon-1-quant at 0% traffic in us-west-2 until we can reproduce and patch kernel selection. Also run a canary of the patched kernel on a small dedicated pool. Long term: add sequence-length routing guard to avoid quant variants with extreme contexts.

maya (oncall): agree. I'm going to mark this as "variant disabled" and handoff to ashley/kevin for next 6 hours. I'll escalate to oncall-rotation if we see re-escalation.

ashley (sre): performing the disable now in control plane:
```
# disable variant in control plane (prevents any routing rules from sending to it)
redwoodctl model update --model=epsilon-1-quant --state=disabled --region=us-west-2 --note="emergency-disable-2140001234"
```

deploy-bot: MODEL_UPDATE: epsilon-1-quant state=disabled (us-west-2).

maya (oncall): status check after traffic shift + disable + quotas:
- 5xx rate (us-west-2 /v2/generate) dropped from 12% -> 0.9% over 3m window
- acme-app error spikes down ~85% from peak
- affected hosts (usw2-ep-03/05/07) no longer receiving traffic; memory error logs stop within 30s of shift

olivia (support): drafting customer note to acme-app: will include timeline, current mitigation (traffic routed to epsilon-stable-v3, temporary throttles), and contact for escalations. ETA for message: 10m.

kevin (eng-runtime): starting a small repro job against epsilon-1-quant on a dedicated dev pool to replicate long-context OOM with the same kernel selection. will avoid touching prod pool.

ashley (sre): recording mitigation steps in incident ticket INC-2140001234. tagging for postmortem: runtime/kernel-selection, model-variant-testing, routing-guards, quota-safety.

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm signed off to sleep in 6m; leaving oncall to ashley (sre) and kevin (eng-runtime). If error rate creeps >2% or model state changes, page oncall immediately.

kevin (eng-runtime): noted. I'll keep a watch on kernel-repro and coordinate with runtime team to revert the recent kernel selection change in the next deploy if repro is confirmed.

santosh (product): I posted a brief for CS. once we have repro and patch plan, let's sync on customer messaging and ETA window.

maya (oncall): thanks team. moving incident -> mitigation-state. follow-up actions:
- ashley: own postmortem doc and exact timeline + impact breakdown (tickets, hit counts)
- kevin: repro + PR for kernel fix + canary plan
- santosh: customer comms and prioritized customer callbacks
- olivia: update support threads with mitigation note and how to request escalation

incident-bot: NOTE: incident INC-2140001234 created and linked. severity: sev2.

maya (oncall): closing active paging. anyone who wants to join the postmortem sync at 09:00 PT tomorrow, please add to calendar.

ashley (sre): adding initial notes to the incident doc now. will append logs and metric screenshots.

kevin (eng-runtime): preliminary finding: new kernel selector returned aggressive prefetch for quant path when seq > 2048. setting up a small patch to gate prefetch behind a config flag + add telemetry.

olivia (support): sent update to acme-app and learnly. both acknowledge and ask for follow-up call; scheduling now.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. incident thread archived to incidents channel but keep updating the incident doc for the postmortem.
